case.title: Air Lead 1 — opening melody
case.method: Hardware-only inspection of a 4096-sample STFT and 70 ms Hann-window FFTs of the opening phrase. Stable fundamental families near 311, 415, 466, 622 and 554 Hz identify sounding MIDI 63, 68, 70, 75 and 73. The published Upper tone has both oscillator coarse bytes 100 (signed +36), WIDE off, hence +12 semitones each; tone octave -1 cancels this, so played and sounding MIDI agree. Transition times come from changes of the fundamental/harmonic family and short RMS dips; note-off at the next onset is a practical estimate. No model parameter fitting.

case.title: Club Bass — separated opening bass reconstruction
case.method: Hardware-only spectrograms show a low D1 family near 36.7 Hz together with components near 73.4 and 293 Hz. The original patch maps a played key to Lower oscillators at −12, Upper triangle at 0, and Upper sine at +24 semitones, so the first three keys are MIDI 38 (D2). Later 43.65/87.3/349 Hz families identify MIDI 41 (F2), followed by two more D2 events. Onsets, repeated-note renewals, and gates were read from the audio waveform and spectral changes without fitting to Septum.

case.method: Hardware-only low-frequency peaks, octave-spaced harmonic families, and amplitude discontinuities identify five opening events. The lower sine and Upper square both sound one octave below the played key; the Upper saw sounds at the played key. The two low E-flat events therefore map to MIDI 39, the octave-up E-flat events to 51, and the final D-flat to 49. The crop stops before the later continuous pitch movement. No Septum rendering was consulted to derive notes or times.

case.title: SupaJuce 1 — two-square oscillator octave check
case.method: Hardware-only FFT/STFT inspection of the first phrase. Lower square fundamentals near 330, 220, 294 and 196 Hz identify sounding MIDI 64, 57, 62 and 55. Undo the published Upper tone octave shift -1 to infer played MIDI 76, 69, 74 and 67. Strong even-numbered families at twice those frequencies, including H6 but not H4, identify the second square one octave above; this is consistent with published OSC1 coarse raw 100/WIDE off and OSC2 raw 64/WIDE off. Onsets and gates estimated from spectral renewals; no synthesis parameter fitting.

case.title: Vangelead — descending fifths
case.method: Hardware-only STFT and Hann-window FFT inspection identifies successive fundamental families near 880, 587, 392, 262 and 175 Hz: MIDI 81, 74, 67, 60 and 53. Both published tones have octave shift 0, both oscillator coarse bytes 64 (signed 0), and WIDE off, so no octave correction is applied. The dual patch supplies layered saw/Super Saw timbre and long tails; continuing old harmonics are treated as patch tails rather than guessed additional held keys. Note changes are placed at the observed spectral renewals/RMS dips. No software rendering or parameter fitting was used.
uncertainties: Original performance MIDI is unavailable. This is an audio-derived estimate, not an original MIDI file.
